messages:
Ravi: Throwing this up as a follow-up to the RFC: propose a "surgical siphon" program — break the largest hot-path coupling points into 8-week slices and extract them with guarded cutovers. goal: shrink blast radius and make ownership clear.
Jo: Love the name. quick ask: can we prioritize by customer-visible latency delta + difficulty? not just code churn.
Ravi: yes. scoring per-slice: (impact * severity) / change-cost. impact = estimated p95 reduction; severity = incident count contribution.
Priya: For data moves we should standardize the pattern. my preference: "read-fanout, write-proxy, backfill" for medium risk. Example backfill command I used recently: `./backfill --slice enricher --from 2024-01-01 --batch 5000`.
Luca: We must keep hot-key locality. If enrichment moves to a different service, the extra round-trip will spike p95. we should measure tail latency delta on worst-100 keys.
Ravi: Plan: week 0-2 spike per slice (prototype + smoke tests), week 3-6 extraction with canary, week 7-8 ramp & monitor. owners assigned per slice.
Jo: Operational gates before ramp: telemetry (token-level cost + latency), error-budget check, and a rollback playbook. No ramps without all three.
Priya: I'll draft a migration playbook template with checklist entries: `dual-write probe`, `backfill idempotency checks`, `consistency validator`, `rollback toggle`, and `customer comms blurb`.
ops-bot: NOTE: Create incident channel automatically when canary p95 increases >20% for 5m. Hook: #inc-automated :zap:
Luca: dev note: for one slice we should try a co-located sidecar to preserve locality. spike will run sidecar on 10% of pods behind a flag and mirror 5% of traffic.
Ravi: Good. owners: Luca -> sidecar spike, Jo -> slice prioritization + metrics dashboard, Priya -> migration playbook + backfill tooling. deliverables after spike: doc, perf matrix, runbook.
Jo: Can we also add a lightweight contract-test harness that runs against both old and extracted paths? golden prompts + fuzzy-tolerance for semantically equivalent responses.
Priya: yes. I'll write a small test harness that runs `golden-suite` and diffs outputs with configurable tolerance. sample config: `tolerance: semantic:0.02, latency-ms:50`.
Ravi: Risk register item: schema churn across services. mitigation: versioned schemas and adapter shims for 3 months.
Luca: small suggestion: add a "reconciliation window" after cutover where we run async validators comparing both stores for drift.
Jo: timeline sanity check: can we do 3 low-risk slices in parallel? assumes 2 spike teams. we should avoid overlapping canaries on same infra.
Ravi: Parallelize only if owners are different and canary windows are staggered. ops will approve schedule.
ops-bot: ACTION: Created ticket INFRA-3345 for canary schedule approval. Link: https://tickets.redwood.internal/INFRA-3345 :white_check_mark:
Priya: I'll prototype backfill and reconciliation tooling this week and post results.
Ravi: Thanks. next step: owners post spike plan docs in this thread by EOD Friday. weekly 30m sync to follow.
